A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAPPS study. The main text, Tables 1–5, Figures 1–4, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAPPS results for crystal generation, structure prediction, bandgap-constrained generation, and workflow validity in Section 4, with bandgap distributions in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original MAPPS experimental results, including all five result tables and the appendix bandgap distributions.

M1.justification: Sections 2.3–2.5 retain the same Workflow Planner, Scientific Mediator, Tool Code Generator, physics tools, and error-driven code revision. The prompts, workflow example, and generated code in Appendix A are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate generation on MP-20 and Matbench, structure prediction on MP-20, MPTS-52 and the challenge set, and bandgap-constrained generation using JARVIS-DFT. The workflow-planning tasks also remain identical.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–3 and 5, including MatLLMSearch for Matbench and CrystaLLM for the challenge set. The newly cited El Agente is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported 1,000-candidate generation setup, one-shot structure prediction, and 500 structures per bandgap condition remain unchanged. Retrieval rules, metrics, thresholds, and the DFT settings in Appendix D are also retained.

E4.justification: Both retain the same with/without-human-intuition analysis in Section 4.4 and Table 5, structure examples in Figures 2–3, and bandgap-distribution analysis in Appendix B. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the reported experiments. Point-estimate and histogram reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the findings illustrated in Figures 2–4 are retained. For example, MAPPS's MP-20 S.U.N. rate remains 24.9%, and high/low-bandgap condition satisfaction remains 74.6%/92.2%.

T1.justification: The crystal representation, probabilistic planning and code-generation equations (1)–(6), and Appendix C metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds proofs, derivations, or formal assumptions relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three-component MAPPS contribution, Level 2 human-guided autonomy claim, and five-fold improvement claim on MP-20. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning expert guidance and current LLM planning limitations remain identical in Section 4.4. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning human involvement and unexplored applications beyond materials discovery.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same OpenAI API and single-A100 setup, Appendix A prompts and CHGNet/ASE code example, and Appendices C–D evaluation details. No implementation parameters or code/data access instructions are added.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zou et al.'s El Agente: An autonomous agent for quantum chemistry as reference [12] in the introduction's discussion of fixed-workflow agents. The substantive related-work discussion and MAPPS positioning remain unchanged; other bibliography revisions concern existing works.

P1.justification: v3 adds a Brookhaven affiliation for Xiaoning Qian and updates bibliographic records, including ChatMOF, CRISPR-GPT, ChemCrow, and the vdW-functional paper. It also removes the duplicate pymatgen entry. Main prose, section order, and appendix organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v3 reduces the large blank space beneath Figure 1, reflows text around existing displays, and adjusts table spacing and Code 1 syntax highlighting. Figure content, axes, captions, and table membership remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves scholarly documentation by adding a relevant citation, providing fuller publication and DOI information for existing references, and removing the duplicate pymatgen record. These are limited editorial gains; the methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility details remain unchanged.
